title: Cost drivers UI exploration (Route + Model usage insights)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Cost drivers UI exploration (Route + Model usage insights)
Exploring: table-first vs visual-first breakdowns; route detail; export placement
Alicia Perez (w/ Tessa Morgan) — Console & Tooling
Last edited: 2026-02-20

Speaker notes:
- This is an exploration deck to align PM/Design/Eng on the “top drivers” experience before we lock the IA and build the first iteration.
- Focus is on: (1) answering “what routes are costing us the most?” quickly, (2) drilling into models + deltas, (3) making exports discoverable but not intrusive.


Slide 2 — Goals / non-goals for the UI iteration
Goals
- Make “Top cost drivers” scannable in <30s (default view works out-of-the-box)
- Clear drill-down path: Route list → Route detail → Model breakdown
- Show changes vs prior period without calling it “anomaly detection”
- Support export for Finance/Ops workflows w/ auditable filters

Non-goals for this pass
- Custom customer-defined dimensions beyond route/model
- Advanced alerting / anomaly rules
- Perfect invoice reconciliation in UI (we’ll message known mismatch reasons)

Speaker notes:
- We should design for day-1 utility: if route tagging is missing, the UI should still help users identify the gap (“Unknown route”).


Slide 3 — Key user questions (from PM + calls + support)
Primary
1) What are my top routes by spend? (and over what time range)
2) Which model(s) drive that spend on a given route?
3) What changed vs last week? (spend + latency + error rate)

Secondary
4) Why doesn’t this match my invoice?
5) Can I export this with the same filters I’m viewing?
6) Can I share/hand off route detail to another team?

Notes / implications
- The list view must include enough context to avoid immediate clicks for every route
- Delta views need clear “compare period” semantics
- Export must preserve filter context + be discoverable from list and detail


Slide 4 — Information architecture options (2 candidates)
Option A (Table-first)
Usage Insights
- Routes (default)
  - Route list (ranked)
  - Route detail
- Models (secondary tab)
  - Model list (ranked)
  - Model detail (later)

Option B (Drivers-first)
Usage Insights
- Cost drivers (default)
  - Treemap / grouped visualization
  - Table beneath
  - Drill into “node” (route or model)

Pros / cons summary
- A: closer to current console patterns; faster to build; works w/ pagination + RBAC boundaries
- B: more “wow” but harder to make precise (filters, sorting, comparisons) and risks being less usable for finance workflows

Speaker notes:
- We can still add a small visualization inside Option A (sparklines + stacked model pill) without going full treemap-first.


Slide 5 — Route list: Table-first (mock layout)
Wireframe (text)
Header:
- Title: “Routes”
- Time range picker (Last 7 days default)
- Compare toggle: “vs previous period” (on by default?)
- Filters: Environment, Region, Deployment mode, Project
- Search box: “Search routes…”
- CTA: Export (primary on right)

Table columns (proposed)
- Route (name + small “tag source” indicator: SDK / Gateway / Unknown)
- Spend (total + % of total)
- Unit cost (e.g., $/1M tokens) (optional column, off by default)
- Tokens (input / output / cached) (expand-on-row)
- Latency p95
- Error rate
- Trend (sparkline)

Row affordances
- Click route name → detail view
- Kebab menu: Copy link; Export for this route; View raw query (internal only?)

Speaker notes:
- Strong bias toward table because it supports scanning + sorting.
- “Tag source” might reduce support load: customers can immediately see if route attribution is coming from SDK or gateway-derived.


Slide 6 — Route list: Table-first (pros/cons)
Pros
- Very legible ranking for “top routes” (finance/ops happy)
- Sorting/pagination aligns with API work (top N + pagination)
- Easy to add “Unknown route” row and message route-tagging setup
- Low risk for accessibility (screen readers, keyboard nav)

Cons / risks
- Table density: many metrics can overwhelm; must choose default columns carefully
- If customers have high cardinality routes, the list can become noisy (need guardrails + rollups)
- Visual hierarchy for “what changed” needs care (avoid making it feel like alerting)

Mitigations
- Column picker + “Compact / Comfortable” density
- Default to 7d; show “Showing top 200 routes” + guidance
- Roll up/hide routes flagged as dynamic (depending on backend policy)


Slide 7 — Route list: Visual-first (Treemap / grouped view)
Wireframe (text)
Top section:
- Treemap grouped by route (area = spend)
- Color = change vs previous period (green down / red up)

Below:
- Table of top routes (same as Option A) for precision

Interactions
- Hover on tile: spend, delta, p95 latency, top model
- Click tile: route detail
- Filter chips apply to both views

Speaker notes:
- We can prototype this quickly but it may not survive contact with real cardinality (lots of tiny tiles) and compare semantics.


Slide 8 — Treemap / visual-first (pros/cons)
Pros
- Immediately shows “big rocks” and relative size distribution
- Can make deltas more discoverable (color)
- Good for exec demos / quick intuition

Cons
- Hard to read with long route names and many routes
- Accessibility + keyboard navigation complexity
- “Compare vs prior period” color encoding can be misleading if spend is low but % change is high
- Precision tasks still require a table (so we’re building both)

Recommendation (design)
- Ship table-first for GA; consider treemap as a later enhancement once we understand customer route distributions


Slide 9 — Drill-down: Route detail (layout)
Route detail header
- Route name + “normalized” indicator (and original if different)
- Filters context summary (env/region/project)
- Time range picker (inherits from list)
- Compare (vs previous period)
- Export for this route

Sections
1) KPI strip
- Spend (total)
- Tokens (in/out/cached)
- p95 latency
- Error rate

2) Spend over time
- Line chart (daily buckets for 7–30d; hourly buckets for 24h)
- Overlay previous period (dotted)

3) Model breakdown
- Table: model variant, spend, tokens, p95 latency, errors, share
- Optional stacked area chart for share over time (later)

4) “What changed” panel
- Top 3 drivers (e.g., spend up due to output tokens +34%; model mix shift from X to Y)
- Links: “See breakdown” anchors to relevant table sections

Speaker notes:
- Keep “What changed” as explanatory, not prescriptive. Avoid “anomaly” language.


Slide 10 — Route detail: Model breakdown visualization options
Option 1: Model table only (default)
- Pros: precise, sortable, easy export parity
- Cons: less intuitive for mix shifts

Option 2: Table + horizontal stacked bar (share)
- Single bar showing model share of spend for selected period
- Pros: quick intuition; low UI complexity
- Cons: still not a time-series

Option 3: Stacked area over time (later)
- Pros: best for identifying routing/fallback changes
- Cons: can be noisy; expensive to render; more query load

Recommendation
- Option 2 for beta/GA (table + share bar), Option 3 behind “Advanced” later


Slide 11 — “What changed” copy + UX patterns
Pattern A: Inline deltas next to KPIs
- Spend: $12,430 (+18%)
- p95 latency: 820ms (+9%)

Pattern B: Dedicated “What changed” card
- “Spend increased +$1,880 (+18%) vs previous 7 days”
- Bullets:
  - Output tokens +22% (largest contributor)
  - Model mix shifted: llama-3.1-70b → llama-3.1-8b-instruct (cost down, latency down)
  - Error rate increased to 1.9% (was 0.8%)

Guardrails
- Always include absolute + relative deltas
- Avoid red/green only; include neutral language (“increased/decreased”)
- Link to support FAQ for invoice mismatch + late data

Speaker notes:
- Deltas are a major value prop but must be careful with customer trust; they’ll cross-check with invoices.


Slide 12 — Filter model (list + detail)
Filters to include in beta/GA
- Time range (required)
- Environment (prod/staging/dev) if available
- Region
- Deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Org + Project (scoped by RBAC; no cross-project leakage)

Filters to defer
- Customer-defined tags
- Request attribute deep cuts (e.g., temperature, max_tokens) unless PM prioritizes later

UX notes
- Filters persist across navigation (Routes → Route detail → back)
- Show “Filters applied” summary for export auditing parity
- Empty state must be specific (e.g., “No route-tagged traffic in this period” vs “No data”)


Slide 13 — Export placement + flow options
Option A: Primary button in header (Routes list + Route detail)
- “Export” button opens modal
- Default export respects current filters (and route if in detail)

Option B: Kebab on each row (Route list)
- “Export this route” available per row

Option C: Separate “Reports” tab
- More powerful but larger scope + adds another mental model

Recommendation
- Option A + B
  - Header export: most common
  - Row export: convenient for chargeback workflows

Export modal (draft content)
- Format: CSV or JSON
- Granularity: hourly/daily (if exposed)
- Limits: show max rows / max days allowed
- “This export will be audit logged” note

Speaker notes:
- Finance workflows often want “same view I’m seeing” exported; modal should reflect the exact filters.


Slide 14 — Empty states / error states
Route list empty states
1) No data due to time range / filters
- Message: “No usage found for this selection.”
- Action: Clear filters / change time range

2) Data exists but route is missing
- Message: “Most requests are currently attributed to ‘Unknown route’.”
- Actions: “Set route identifiers” (docs link), “View Unknown route details”

3) Insights delayed
- Message: “Data is still processing (up to X minutes).”
- Show last updated timestamp

Errors
- API timeout: show retry + reduce time range suggestion
- Permission denied: “You don’t have access to this project’s usage insights.”

Notes
- These states reduce support tickets (SUP-18441 style “Unknown route dominating”).


Slide 15 — Cardinality considerations that affect UI
Observed risk
- Customer routes can be dynamic (user IDs, UUIDs, long query strings)
- Leads to massive lists, poor ranking, confusing exports

UI implications (even if backend enforces)
- Display normalized route (and optionally “original” on hover) if we apply normalization
- Consider warning badges:
  - “High cardinality route pattern detected” (only if we can reliably detect)
- Consider “Other” bucket in ranking (“Other routes (rolled up)”) if backend provides

Design question
- Do we want to expose “route normalization applied” as a concept in UI? (Pros: transparency; Cons: adds cognitive load)


Slide 16 — Design feedback notes (from review 2026-02-18)
Attendees
- Tessa (Design), Paula (PM), Felix (Console), Dylan (Console eng sponsor), Nadia (Telemetry), Allison (SRE reviewer)

Feedback highlights
- Strong preference for table-first for GA (“finance must be able to sort + export reliably”)
- Route detail: keep model breakdown above fold; don’t hide it behind an accordion
- Export button: keep top-right in header; avoid burying in kebab only
- Add “last updated” timestamp and/or “data freshness” note (SRE request)
- Avoid too many default columns; ship a sane default and allow a column picker later if needed

Open questions
- Should we default compare toggle ON? (PM leaning yes, Design leaning no)
- Do we show cached tokens as separate KPI by default? (Nadia: yes for cost; PM: maybe in tooltip)


Slide 17 — Recommendation (what we build first)
MVP recommendation
- Routes list: table-first ranked by spend (sortable), with sparklines + basic filters
- Route detail: KPIs + spend trend + model breakdown table + simple “what changed” summary
- Export: header button on list + detail; row action “export this route”

Defer
- Treemap/visual-first as default
- Stacked area chart by model over time
- Dedicated “Reports” section

Rationale
- Ships core customer value faster and maps cleanly to planned backend APIs
- Lowest risk for accessibility + high-cardinality environments


Slide 18 — Next steps / asks
Next steps (Design)
- Confirm default columns + the KPI strip (by 2026-02-24)
- Draft empty states copy + docs links (“Unknown route” guidance)

Next steps (Eng)
- Validate table density/perf with expected top-N + pagination constraints
- Confirm what fields are available for “tag source” (SDK vs gateway) and if we can surface it

PM asks
- Decide compare default behavior + how we label “previous period”
- Confirm GA acceptance criteria for export discoverability

References
- Linear DES-211, ENG-8426/8427
- Confluence design spec: console-usage-insights-route-model-breakdown
- ADR: route dimension definition + normalization
